The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Shadow With the Wrong Hat

Chip had promised to show visitors the turn toward Everybody Day. He found a fine landmark. A sunflower cast a shadow across the path that looked exactly like a lady in a big floppy hat.

“Turn at the hat!” he told Toad that morning. Toad did. He arrived at the birdhouse without a single wrong hop. Chip drew a fine floppy hat on his paper leaf.

“Turn at the hat,” he told Beetle after lunch. Beetle came back with a thistle burr on his head. “I found a hat,” he said. “I am wearing it. Where exactly should I turn?”

They went back together. The sunflower was still there. Its shadow had stretched clear across the ditch. The lady in the hat appeared to be going for a swim.

“Maybe something that stays put?” Beetle suggested. Chip looked for the sunflower itself. From beetle height all he could see was a long green leg. Then his beak bumped a stone. It had two bumpy neighbors.

Chip turned the paper leaf over. He drew the three bumps close together. Beetle tried the turn. Daisy tried it too, hopping instead of flying. Then a cloud covered the sun. The bumps were still quite bumpy.

Chip hung the stone picture on the Welcome Tree for visitors to copy. On the back he kept the fancy hat. “For parties,” he explained. Beetle decided his burr was a bit itchy and returned it to the thistles.

That evening Chip walked past the sunflower. Its long shadow reached all the way to his toes. He lifted an imaginary hat. The sunflower nodded, which was very polite of it.

Read together

What would help you find the same turn on a cloudy day?
